summary.one_liner: A curated awesome-list of web archiving resources, covering training materials, WARC tools, crawlers, replay engines, search tools, and public archive datasets.
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome" list of links rather than a single software project. It is organized into sections: training and documentation, resources for web publishers, tools and software (acquisition, replay, search and discovery, utilities, WARC I/O libraries, analysis, quality assurance, curation), community resources (other lists, blogs, mailing lists, chat servers, social accounts), web archiving service providers, and public data sources. Many tool entries carry a status tag such as Stable or In Development. The list covers crawlers like Browsertrix Crawler, Heritrix, and grab-site, replay engines like pywb and ReplayWeb.page, and WARC libraries such as warcio and jwarc. It also points to public WARC and CDX datasets such as Common Crawl and the End of Term Archive.
use_cases: find a web crawler for archiving websites to WARC
replay archived WARC or WACZ files in a browser
learn web archiving concepts and the WARC standard
locate open datasets of archived web pages
save single-page copies of web pages as HTML
search and analyze large web archive collections
stack: Tools listed span Python, Java, Go, Rust, Node.js, and JavaScript
notable: Covers the full web archiving lifecycle, from acquisition and replay to analysis and curation
Each tool is tagged with a maturity status such as Stable or In Development
Includes a Public Data section listing downloadable WARCs, CDX APIs, and indexes
Lists self-hostable and hosted service providers, noting which export WARC or WACZ
caveats: This is a link list, so it does not itself provide software; each entry must be checked separately
The README notes that Conifer's hosted service was discontinued in June 2026
Some entries are marked In Development and may be incomplete or unmaintained
